key_concepts: Weathering breaks rocks into smaller pieces
Hammering rock models rock breakdown by force
Inflating a balloon under notebooks models expansion pressure in rock cracks
Rubbing sandpaper on rock models abrasion
Pouring water from height models water as a weathering agent
Vinegar on chalk models acid breaking down rocks
Water, wind, and ice are agents of erosion
Soil forms in layers called horizons
O horizon is the organic layer and A horizon is topsoil with microorganisms and worms
E horizon is the leaching layer and B horizon is subsoil
C horizon is substratum and R horizon is bedrock at the bottom
Models can represent weathering, erosion, and soil profile layers
